summary: Join our comprehensive training course on Gender Mainstreaming in Humanitarian Programs. Equip yourself with essential skills to foster inclusivity and equality
lede: Gender mainstreaming in humanitarian programs helps teams consider how crises affect access, safety, and participation. For people who plan, deliver, fund, or evaluate humanitarian assistance, the course builds practical skills in rapid gender analysis, integrating gender considerations across the program cycle, and reducing GBV and protection risks through safer, more inclusive programming.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for those engaged in designing, funding, reporting, or evaluating humanitarian assistance, including:
audience: Protection, GBV, and child protection staff
Sector leads (WASH, Shelter, Health, Nutrition, Education
Government disaster management and social services staff
modules: Gender Mainstreaming in Humanitarian Action: What It Really Means
Gender Across the Humanitarian Program Cycle
Gender in Targeting and Vulnerability Criteria
GBV Risk Mitigation and Safe Programming
Gender and AAP: Participation, Feedback, and Complaints
Sector Applications: WASH, Shelter, Health, Nutrition, EiE, and Cash
Gender Markers, Donor Requirements, and Proposal Quality
Gender-Sensitive MEAL: Indicators, Data, and Learning
Coordination and Partnering for Gender Results
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of humanitarian principles and experience in program design or implementation in humanitarian contexts.
